title: Test Quality and Reliability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Test Quality and Reliability”?
options: Test Quality and Reliability helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Test Quality and Reliability means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Test Quality and Reliability removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Test Quality and Reliability should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Test Quality and Reliability helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Test Quality and Reliability is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Deterministic test data” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Deterministic test data” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Deterministic test data” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Deterministic test data” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Deterministic test data” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Deterministic test data” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Deterministic test data” under Test Quality and Reliability. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Test Quality and Reliability”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
